Daily Transit Intelligence
June 26, 2026 — 15 papers analyzed
KEY FINDINGS
Plainclothes fare inspectors detect about 26% more evaders per hour than
uniformed ones in a 21,727-record Swiss causal-ML study, reversing the visible-
deterrence assumption behind most fare enforcement programs.
A 972-instance benchmark on real Dutch and Swiss rail networks finds the textbook
"exact" line-planning model fails at scale, while a compact approximation wins on
83% of large instances.
Rider satisfaction is best predicted by a Minimum-End heuristic -- the worst moment
plus the ending -- not average experience, across 2,576 real German transit trips,
challenging standard satisfaction-survey design.
PAPER OF THE DAY
Line Planning at Scale: Models, Methods, and Insights
Rolf van Lieshout, Bart van Rossum
Across 972 test cases on real Dutch and Swiss rail networks, the textbook-standard exact
transfer model for line planning loses to a simpler, compact approximation as soon as networks
get large.
It's the most consequential contrarian finding in the batch for working transit planners: a
